To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the formation of local Al rear contacts in PERC solar cells is influenced by a non-uniform firing temperature and that the BSF thickness is correlated to the temperature distribution.
the temperature distribution on the Si wafter is a critical parameter for the formation of local rear Al contacts.
the temperature distribution during the co-firings of Al and Ag paste has a strong impact on the local contact properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the influence of thermal non-unifomity on local contact formation in PERC structures and their impact on electrical and optical properties.
a detailed investigation of the influence of thermal non-unifomity during the firing process on the formation of local Al contacts and their impact on electrical properties of PERC cells.
the investigation of the temperature distribution on the Si-wafer and the impact on the Al-paste.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
local Al contacts with a well-defined Al-paste and a well-defined belt furnace temperature profile are the key for an excellent contact formation.
the formation of voids in local Al contacts is a result of the combination of a non-optimal Al paste and a thermal non-uniform temperature distribution on the Si waffer.
a uniform firing temperature is the key for a high quality rear contact formation and thus, the most important factor to achieve high quality rear contacts in PERC cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of the presented methods is very helpful to investigate local contacts and the influence of thermal non-unifomity on the contact formation.
the temperature uniformity of the wafer during co-firing process has a major impact on the electrical performance of a PERC solar cell.
the combination of SAM, IV and EL measurements is a very powerful method to detect and analyze local defects in PERC solar cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
local rear contacts are not only influenced by local Al thickness but also by local temperature distribution.
the temperature uniformity on the wafer has a strong impact on the formation of the local rear contacts and the resulting electrical properties of the PERC solar cells.
the combination of SAM and EL imaging is an efficient tool to determine voids spatially resolved in PERC cells.
